label: R4233, fr. 3053 f. 6 ff., Rome, 26 Jan 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
sample_original: Le Roy n'est pour faire chose qui soit indigne de son nom. Le bonhomme se porte bien, mais il est septuagenaire et plus, et ne peult esperer davantaige que d'un homme vieil et caduc.
sample_en: The King will do nothing unworthy of his name. The old man is well, but he is seventy or more and can hope for no more than from an old and feeble man.
why: Continuous 16th-c. French running reading with clear-text passages summarised; the open groups (about 100 of 2,006 letters) are scattered, a few per paragraph, and sentences stay whole.

label: R4234, fr. 3053 ff. 16r-18v, Rome, Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
sample_original: Il est vray, Monseigneur, que ce sont advis grandement importans, mais me tenant les propoz que faict Sa Saincteté, il me semble, soubz [?] correction, qu'il n'est bon en monstrer semblant a monsieur le cardinal de Carpi
sample_en: It is true, my lord, that these are very important advices, but given what His Holiness says, it seems to me, subject to correction, that it is not good to show any sign of it to Cardinal Carpi.
why: f. 17r-17v and 18v build whole sentences, but f. 16r and especially f. 16v carry a [?] or (?) in nearly every clause ('grande [?] ment [?] des advantaiges(?) [?] aide duce don[?]'), and f. 18r is mostly elided clear-copy summary with '...'.

label: R4235, fr. 3053 f. 21 ff., Rome, 15 Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
sample_original: le pape tend affin d'avoir les fortes places du duché de Milan entre ses mains, donnant a entendre luy avoir esté dict de la part du Roy, chose qui n'est poinct procedée de ma bouche.
sample_en: The pope aims to get the strongholds of the duchy of Milan into his hands, giving it to be understood that he was told so on the King's behalf, which did not come from my mouth.
why: Coherent running French, about 95 % of letters read; holes are single '[?]' groups here and there, and the reading is translatable as it stands.

label: R4238, fr. 3053 ff. 32v-33r, Rome, [xiii?] Sept 1536
sample_original: Ce porteur est envoié par les forussiz de Siennes devers le Roy, pour luy persuader de vouloir faire entreprise au dict Siennes.
sample_en: This bearer is sent by the Sienese exiles to the King, to persuade him to make an enterprise against Siena.
why: Short letter read in full; the only holes are German proper names (surname of Christofle, two captains), sentences are whole.

label: R4239, fr. 3053 ff. 35r-38v, Rome, 6 Apr 1537
sample_original: Le seigneur Pierre Luis m'a faict dire soubz main par l'evesque de Cesane, depuis m'avoir parlé, qu'il luy a esté faict de nouveau [offre], que les imperiaulx le poursuivoient de l'accepter [Novara]
sample_en: Pier Luigi had the bishop of Cesena tell me privately, after speaking to me, that a new offer had been made to him and that the Imperials urged him to accept it [Novara].
why: Letter 2 (f. 36r-v) reads in long whole sentences; the Letter 1 running reading (f. 35r-v) is a summary with '...' elisions inside most sentences ('qu'il estime que ... ou l'octroi ou le refuz: s'il octroie, pour s'en servir a entretenir le don au Roy ...'), and the clear passages are not written out.

label: R4240, fr. 3053 f. 40r-v, Orvieto, 2 Sept 1536

sample_en: As to which I have it on good authority that the Germans will never consent, for they say the morals of the pope, cardinals and bishops need reforming.
why: One paragraph of cipher read at 98.5 % of letters; two small holes only. Fully translatable.

label: Forster papers, 13 May 1644
sample_original: Prenez seulement les voies de prudence pour conserver votre vie, pour en faire à Dieu un plus grand sacrifice par la multiplication de vos services pour le salut de vos frères
sample_en: Take only the ways of prudence to preserve your life, so as to make God a greater sacrifice through the multiplication of your services for the salvation of your brothers.
why: A single short note, read in full with Pitt's key; the unspaced decode is followed by a normalised French sentence, with slips and variant readings stated.

label: R932, to General Goring, 5 June 1645
sample_original: Noane inform him wee are strongly beseidged on all sides; if his Highnes doe not give us releif shortly wee shall perish.
sample_en: (already English) Inform him we are strongly besieged on all sides; if His Highness does not relieve us shortly we shall perish.
why: Lasry's plaintext, copied; one short letter with a single unresolved code group and 'Noane' for 'none'/'pray'. Whole sentences.

label: Hamburg, 4/14 May 1672, HStAM 4 f Dänemark Nr. 125, ff. 2-4
sample_original: dass Frankreich mit Schweden geschlossen und Dennemarck vorbeygangen, gibt Verdruss.
sample_en: That France has concluded [an alliance] with Sweden and passed Denmark by gives offence.
why: Only cipher parts are given: a patchwork of excerpts joined by '...', with the codes written as <number name> and a '??' run; individual clauses read well (the Brandenburg and Foedus Dano-Brunsvicense passages) but there is no connected letter, and the clear context is missing.

label: R1156, Pozsony, 1 June 1482
sample_original: Scripsimus regi Ferdinando ... In crastinum hinc recedet Mager Balas capitaneus noster cum pluribus gentibus, iturus in Croatiam versus confinia Venetorum
sample_en: Tomorrow our captain Magyar Balázs will leave here with many men, going to Croatia towards the Venetian border.
why: Good 15th-c. Latin, but the cipher runs are bracketed word by word ('[mittere] in [subsidium] [vestrum] [quingentos]'), clear passages are elided with '…' in lines 1, 5 and 8, and the printed Fraknói text (OCR) is the only complete wording. Reads, but needs reassembling.

label: La Rochelle, 10 July 1586 (BnF 500 de Colbert 401 f. 333)
sample_original: LE ROY DE NAVARRE A ENVOYÉ COMME VOUS SAVEZ LE SR DE VESIN DE LA MARSILLIERE A BERNE AVEC LES AMBASSADEURS DES QUATRE CANTONS DE SUISSE
sample_en: The King of Navarre sent, as you know, the Sieur de Vesin de la Marsilliere to Berne with the ambassadors of the four Swiss cantons.
why: Verbatim script output: the clear text in capitals and the normalised cipher stretches read as French, but the cipher runs are unspaced and misdecoded in places ('sreistresmarcherontilmonteraadhevai', 'etqiiro etleuradviusurlecheminnaldoittenir') and name codes are {162}, {204}...; roughly half the sentences have a hole.

label: Lord Maltravers to Ormonde, 13 Sept 1634 and 22 Jan 1634/5 (HMC Ormonde I pp. 28-29)
sample_original: [Ormonde's] Lord Deputy hath written unto Secretary Coke much in praise of Ormonde in general, and particularly for his good carriage in Parliament, and upon his motion Ormonde is to be a Councellor
sample_en: (already English) The Lord Deputy has written to Secretary Coke praising Ormonde, especially his conduct in Parliament, and on his recommendation he is to be a councillor.
why: Only the cipher passages are given, with nulls marked and code values glossed; the English is clear. Whole letters are not shown, so this is an extract (about a dozen lines), but what is shown reads.

label: Venetian ambassador at Rome to the Doge, 29 April 1628, ASVe Busta 27 f. 354 (DECODE R1862)
sample_original: Opportunissima occ.ne ho io havuta hieri col cardinal Barberino di parlargli di quel negotio che la Ecc.ma mi ha commesso con cotesto Ecc.mo conseglio
sample_en: I had a most opportune occasion yesterday to speak to Cardinal Barberini about that business which Your Excellency entrusted to me with this Excellent Council.
why: Italian ambassador's despatch in per-line unspaced lowercase (P1 L02 'lbarberinodiparlarglidi'), no punctuation, 12 unread groups [nnnn] in 126 lines and some clear passages in braces. The sentences are all there and can be re-divided; needs normalising, not more cryptanalysis.

label: R7475, pp. 29-30, c. 1707
file: texts/R7475_decryption.md (contemporary interlinear gloss with transcriber notes)
sample_original: iednak oba wlaiac sie zeby utrusque iuris doctores sub specie amicitiae nie wprowadzili w mm pana y rempublicam in discrimen irreparabile
sample_en: however, [be wary] lest the doctors of both laws, under the guise of friendship, lead your lordship and the Republic into irreparable danger.
why: Polish-Latin macaronic text line by line, with the transcriber's bracketed notes after most lines (cipher slips, sign counts); old spelling and no diacritics. The prose is coherent and a Polish reader can translate it, but the notes interrupt it and word breaks cut across lines.

label: R4921, BL Add MS 18983 f. 14, Oxford, 29 April 1645
sample_original: therefore I desire you to march speedily for my assistance, that in case I can not bring my train of artillery to you, you may come and fetch it
sample_en: (already English) Therefore I ask you to march speedily to help me, so that if I cannot bring my artillery to you, you may come and fetch it.
why: One letter read as a continuous paragraph; a few bracketed group numbers and one '[?]' remain, and the sense is clear and historically checked.

label: No. 13 (R4801), a letter on the Pope and Bologna, [1527-1529] (George Lasry)
sample_original: et quest per che al peggio non si ha sinon a rendere et tutto si lassa in la discretissima consideratione di V. S. Illustrissima
sample_en: and this because at worst one has only to give back, and all is left to the most discreet consideration of Your Illustrious Lordship.
why: Lasry's decipherment is a single 16th-c. Italian passage with abbreviation brackets (p[er], no[n]) and line breaks from the PDF; most clauses read, though a few spots stay obscure ('la fada bada', 'si piflio'), so it needs normalising and a careful translation.

label: Cardinal Soglia to the nuncio Viale Prelà, Rome, 15 June 1848 (L'Italia del Popolo no. 40)
sample_original: Tuttavia per nuove sopraggiunte circostanze Le partecipo [8093][8102] del (Padre) che Ella rimanga in Inspruck presso l'Imperatore e ovunque egli fosse per recarsi
sample_en: However, because of new circumstances, I inform you [...] of the Holy Father that you remain at Innsbruck with the Emperor and wherever he may go.
why: One dispatch; the first two sentences carry five and three unread [8xxx] groups and parenthesised guessed code words, so the opening is a skeleton; the later sentences (Innsbruck, Morichini) read whole. The English rendering itself uses '[…]' in four places.
